mainTopic: Mixtures with things from an אשרה, nullifying idols and their broken pieces, and stones next to מרקוליס
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה about wood taken from an אשרה. The wood is forbidden for benefit, and so is a new oven heated with it, bread baked with it, and a garment woven with a shuttle made from it. If these get mixed with others, the רבנן forbid everything. רבי אליעזר lets you throw the value into ים המלח instead. The גמרא explains why both the bread case and the shuttle case were needed. It then rules like רבי אליעזר, and רב אדא בר אהבה and רב חסדא argue whether this also works for a barrel of יין נסך. A new משנה teaches how a gentile nullifies an אשרה by taking even a leaf from it. The גמרא then discusses the shavings of the tree, and רב and שמואל argue about an idol that broke. After the הדרן for פרק כל הצלמים, a new פרק begins with stones lying next to מרקוליס. The גמרא explains that the argument between רבי ישמעאל and חכמים is only about stones whose origin is unknown.

steps.title: Wood from an אשרה and things made with it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that wood from an אשרה is forbidden for benefit. A new oven heated with it must be smashed, an old oven must be cooled, and bread baked with it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone took wood from an אשרה, the wood is forbidden for benefit. If he heated an oven with it: if the oven is new, it must be smashed; if it is old, it must be cooled down. If he baked bread with it, the bread is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule: wood from an אשרה is forbidden. That ban also spreads to things that got benefit from the wood, like an oven or bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating a new oven for the first time hardens it, so the benefit from the forbidden wood stays inside the oven for good, and the oven must be smashed. An old oven only gets a passing benefit from the heat, so cooling it down is enough. Bread baked with the forbidden fire got its whole existence from the forbidden wood, so the bread is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to get any benefit from (not just forbidden to eat)
He heated / lit a fire in

phrases.english: MISHNAH
If one took wood from it —
phrases.notes: "It" is the אשרה, the worshipped tree the earlier משנה was talking about.

phrases.english: they are forbidden for benefit.
If he heated the oven with them,
if it is new, it must be smashed,
and if it is old, it must be cooled.
If he baked bread with it —
it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood from an אשרה is forbidden for benefit, and so is anything that got lasting benefit from it: a new oven heated with it (smash it), an old oven (cool it), and bread baked with it.

steps.title: Forbidden bread mixed with other bread
steps.stepSummary: If the forbidden bread gets mixed with other loaves, all of them are forbidden. רבי אליעזר says you can throw the value of the benefit into ים המלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that bread got mixed with other loaves, all of them are forbidden for benefit. רבי אליעזר says: he should take the value of the benefit and throw it into ים המלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a mixture case. The first opinion (the רבנן) forbids every loaf, and רבי אליעזר offers a way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we cannot tell which loaf is the forbidden one, the first opinion forbids them all. רבי אליעזר says you only need to destroy money equal to the benefit taken from the forbidden wood. Once the benefit is gone, all the loaves are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He should take away the value of the benefit
The Dead Sea, where things are thrown so nobody can ever use them

phrases.english: If it got mixed with others —
phrases.notes: The forbidden loaf got mixed in with other, permitted loaves.

phrases.english: they are all forbidden for benefit.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should take the benefit to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: He means money equal to what the forbidden wood was worth, thrown away so nobody gains from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the forbidden bread from step 1 and asks what happens when it is mixed with other bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן forbid the whole mixture. רבי אליעזר permits it once the value of the forbidden benefit is thrown into ים המלח.

steps.title: The רבנן reject redemption for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer רבי אליעזר that there is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back against רבי אליעזר's solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's idea works like 'redeeming' the forbidden item by putting its value onto money. The רבנן say that kind of exchange works for some holy things, but not for עבודה זרה. Its ban cannot be moved onto money, so the mixture stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: transferring an item's status onto money
Idol worship and the items connected to it

phrases.english: They said to him:
There is no redemption for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אֵין פִּדְיוֹן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי אליעזר's suggestion in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's method of permitting the mixture.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His method is really a form of redemption, and עבודה זרה cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: A weaving shuttle from an אשרה and the garment woven with it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats the same pattern with a shuttle (כרכור) made from the אשרה. The shuttle and the garment woven with it are forbidden, a mixture is forbidden, and the same dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone took a shuttle from the אשרה, it is forbidden for benefit. If he wove a garment with it, the garment is forbidden for benefit. If it got mixed with other garments, and those got mixed with others, all of them are forbidden. רבי אליעזר says: he should take the benefit to ים המלח. They said to him: There is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case with the same structure: a weaving tool from the אשרה, a garment made with it, a mixture, and the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the forbidden wood is not burned up. It stays whole as the shuttle. Even so, the garment is forbidden because it was made with the forbidden tool. Even a mixture within a mixture stays forbidden according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And the others mixed with yet others (a mixture within a mixture)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is just repeating itself. The גמרא is about to explain why both the bread case and the shuttle case were needed.

phrases.english: If he took a shuttle from it —
it is forbidden for benefit.
If he wove the garment with it —
it is forbidden for benefit.
If it got mixed with others
and the others with others —
phrases.notes: The mixed pile then got mixed again with more garments.

phrases.english: they are all forbidden for benefit.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should take the benefit to the Dead Sea.
They said to him:
There is no redemption for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern as steps 1-3 to a new case, where the forbidden object still exists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shuttle from an אשרה and a garment woven with it are forbidden. Mixtures are forbidden, with the same dispute about throwing the value into ים המלח.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives two parallel cases. In the bread case, the forbidden wood is burned up. In the shuttle case, the forbidden wood is still there. Both carry the same dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: the bread case alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכא. If we only had the bread case, we might think רבי אליעזר is lenient only there, because the forbidden wood has burned up. With the shuttle, which still exists, he might agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Both cases are needed. If the משנה had taught us only the first case, we would say רבי אליעזר rules this way only there, because by the time the bread is finished, the forbidden wood has burned away. But with a shuttle, where the forbidden item still exists as it was, I might say he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה repeated the dispute twice. This is the first half of the explanation: why the bread case alone would not have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the bread case, the forbidden wood is already gone once the bread is baked, so it is easier to permit the bread with a money fix. In the shuttle case, the forbidden wood still exists, so we might have thought even רבי אליעזר would be strict. The shuttle case teaches that רבי אליעזר is lenient even there.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to teach both cases)
Still existing in its original form

steps.confusionAlert: This is only half of the צריכא. The other half, explaining why the shuttle case alone would not be enough, comes in step 6.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: Both the bread case and the shuttle case had to be taught.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us only the first one,
it is in this case that Rabbi Eliezer says so,
because at the time the bread is finished,
the forbidden item has burned away.
But a shuttle,
where the forbidden item still exists as it was,
I might say he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה needed both the bread case (steps 1-3) and the shuttle case (step 4).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread case alone would suggest רבי אליעזר is lenient only when the forbidden wood is already burned up. The shuttle case is needed to show he is lenient even when the forbidden item still exists.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether the forbidden item still exists might matter for how lenient we can be with a mixture. The צריכא tells us רבי אליעזר's view applies in both situations.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed the bread case too
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had only taught the shuttle, we might think the רבנן forbid only there, and agree with רבי אליעזר about bread. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had only taught the shuttle, we would say that only in that case do the רבנן say it is forbidden. But with bread, I might say they agree with רבי אליעזר. So both cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא from step 5 by showing the other direction, then concludes that both cases had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said: from bread alone, we might think רבי אליעזר is lenient only where the wood burned up. Now the reverse: from the shuttle alone, we might think the רבנן are strict only where the wood still exists, and agree to be lenient with bread. Since each case alone could mislead us, the משנה needed both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning both cases had to be taught
The shuttle used for weaving cloth

steps.whatToRemember: The shuttle case shows רבי אליעזר is lenient even when the forbidden wood still exists. The bread case shows the רבנן are strict even when the forbidden wood has burned up. Each case teaches something the other could not.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the shuttle,
in this case the Rabbis say it is forbidden,
but in the case of bread —
I might say they agree with Rabbi Eliezer.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכא begun in step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the bread case and the shuttle case are needed to show how wide the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן really is.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of רב חייא, רב חסדא, and זעירי, the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא the son of רבה בר נחמני said in the name of רב חסדא, who said in the name of זעירי: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in the dispute. We follow רבי אליעזר, so a mixture can be permitted by throwing away the value of the forbidden item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the dispute from the משנה in practice, even though רבי אליעזר is one opinion against the רבנן. The ruling comes through a chain of three אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line: the mixture of bread or garments can be permitted by throwing the value into ים המלח.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rabba bar Naḥmani, said
that Rav Ḥisda said that Ze'eiri said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה to deciding the practical law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר: a mixture can be permitted by throwing away the value of the forbidden item.

steps.title: Another version of who passed down the ruling
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב חסדא heard זעירי's ruling from אבא בר רב חסדא. The ruling itself is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רב חסדא said, אבא בר רב חסדא told me that this is what זעירי said: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how זעירי's ruling reached רב חסדא. The ruling does not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב חסדא quotes זעירי directly. In this version, רב חסדא heard it through אבא בר רב חסדא. The only difference is the chain of who said it, not the law.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion or an argument. Both versions say the same thing: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי אַבָּא בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Abba bar Rav Ḥisda said to me,
this is what Ze'eiri said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different chain of transmission for the same ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same ruling, different chain: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה limits the ruling to bread
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the ruling like רבי אליעזר applies only to bread, not to a barrel of יין נסך mixed with other barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: they taught this only about bread. But a barrel of wine, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה sets a limit on the ruling we just learned. Throwing away the value works for bread, but not for a mixed-up barrel of forbidden wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling like רבי אליעזר was stated about the משנה's bread case. רב אדא בר אהבה says it does not reach a barrel of יין נסך, so a mixture with that barrel stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel, here a barrel of יין נסך

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
They taught this only about bread,
phrases.notes: "This" means the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: but a barrel — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the ruling in steps 7 and 8 reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling like רבי אליעזר applies to bread, but not to a barrel of יין נסך.

steps.title: רב חסדא says even a barrel is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with רב אדא בר אהבה and holds that even a mixed-up barrel of יין נסך can be permitted this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: even a barrel is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא argues with רב אדא בר אהבה. He holds that the method of throwing away the value works even for a barrel of forbidden wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה limited רבי אליעזר's method to bread. רב חסדא gives the method its full reach, so the other barrels become permitted once the value of the forbidden barrel is thrown away.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
Even a barrel is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ חָבִית מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב אדא בר אהבה's limit in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a mixed-up barrel of יין נסך is permitted by throwing away its value.

steps.title: רב חסדא rules for a man whose wine got mixed
steps.stepSummary: A man's wine got mixed with a barrel of יין נסך. רב חסדא told him to throw four זוז into the river, and then the wine would be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whose wine got mixed with a barrel of יין נסך. He came before רב חסדא. רב חסדא said: take four זוז, throw them into the river, and the wine will be permitted to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רב חסדא actually ruling by his own opinion from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the barrel case that רב אדא בר אהבה said is not permitted. רב חסדא puts his view into practice: the four זוז stand for the value of the forbidden barrel, and throwing them away permits the rest of the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured as an offering to עבודה זרה, which is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא holds that רבי אליעזר's method works even for a barrel of יין נסך, and he ruled that way in a real case.
steps.whyThisMatters: A real ruling by רב חסדא shows that his opinion was put into practice and was not only theory.

phrases.english: There was a certain man

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיתְעָרַב לֵיהּ חָבִיתָא דְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ בְּחַמְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: whose wine got mixed with a barrel of libation wine.
He came before Rav Ḥisda.
He said: Take four zuz
phrases.notes: The four זוז stand for the value of the forbidden barrel.

phrases.english: and throw them into the river,
and it will be permitted to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאִיתְעָרַב לֵיהּ חָבִיתָא דְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב חסדא applying his step-10 opinion in a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixture with a barrel of יין נסך becomes permitted by throwing away the value of the forbidden barrel.

steps.title: How a gentile nullifies an אשרה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a gentile nullifies an אשרה by cutting anything from it for his own use, even a single leaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one nullify it? If a gentile trimmed dry wood or cut green branches from the tree, or took a stick, a rod, or even a leaf from it, the tree is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It explains how an אשרה can lose its status as עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the gentile takes something from the tree for his own use, he treats it like an ordinary tree. That shows he no longer worships it, so it becomes בטלה. Even something as small as a leaf is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifies it, so it loses its idol status

phrases.english: MISHNA: How does one nullify it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the אשרה, the worshipped tree from the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: If he trimmed dry wood or pruned green branches,
or took from it a stick or a rod,
even a leaf, it is nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves away from the יין נסך discussion to the nullification of an אשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking even a leaf from an אשרה for one's own use nullifies it.

steps.title: Shaving the tree for its sake or not
steps.stepSummary: If the tree was shaved to improve it, it stays forbidden. If it was shaved for another purpose, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he shaved it down for its own sake, it is forbidden. If not for its own sake, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case: shaving the tree. The result depends on why it was shaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving the tree to make it look nicer honors the idol, so it remains forbidden. Shaving it for some other reason treats it as ordinary wood, so it becomes permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the endings: לְצׇרְכָּהּ means for the idol's sake, while later לְצׇרְכּוֹ means for the person's own sake. One letter changes the whole law.

phrases.english: If he shaved it for its sake, it is forbidden;
phrases.notes: "For its sake" means to benefit the tree itself, like making it look nicer.

phrases.english: not for its sake, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a case where the purpose of the act matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaving for the tree's sake leaves it forbidden. Shaving for any other purpose permits it.

steps.title: What about the shavings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the status of the shavings that came off when the tree was shaved for its own sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those shavings, what is their status?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks a question the משנה did not answer, which sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the tree stays forbidden when shaved for its sake. It did not say whether the pieces that fell off are also forbidden. That gap is what the גמרא wants to fill.

keyTerms.meaning: What will be with them, meaning what is their status

phrases.english: GEMARA: Those shavings,
phrases.notes: He means the shavings from the case where the tree was shaved for its own sake.

phrases.english: what is their status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail the משנה in step 13 left open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the shavings from a tree shaved for its own sake forbidden or permitted?

steps.title: רב הונא and רבי חייא בר רב disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about the shavings. One says they are forbidden, and one says they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רבי חייא בר רב disagree about it. One says they are forbidden, and one says they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two אמוראים argue about the question just asked. It does not tell us which one held which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side treats the shavings like the tree, which is still forbidden. The other side holds that the shavings are permitted even though the tree itself stays forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב הוּנָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav disagree about it:
one says they are forbidden,
and one says they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב הוּנָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by showing that the question is under dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the shavings are forbidden or permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the view that the shavings are permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when a gentile shaves the idol for its sake, the idol is forbidden but the shavings are permitted. When a Jew shaves it, both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports the one who says they are permitted. If a gentile shaved an idol for his own sake, it and its shavings are permitted. If he shaved it for its sake, it is forbidden, but its shavings are permitted. If a Jew shaved an idol, whether for its sake or his own, it and its shavings are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs the view that the shavings are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle case answers our question: a gentile shaved the idol for its sake, and the ברייתא says the idol is forbidden but the shavings are permitted. The ברייתא also adds that a Jew's shaving never nullifies anything, so in his case everything stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the one who says
Whether for its sake or for his sake

steps.whatToRemember: A gentile who shaves for his own needs nullifies the idol. If he shaves for the idol's sake, the idol stays forbidden but the shavings are permitted. When a Jew shaves an idol, both it and the shavings stay forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that only a gentile can nullify an idol. A Jew's actions cannot remove its forbidden status.

phrases.english: It is taught in line with the one who says they are permitted,
as it is taught:
a gentile who shaved an idol for his own sake,
it and its shavings are permitted;
for its sake, it is forbidden but its shavings are permitted.
And a Jew who shaved an idol,
whether for its sake or for his own sake,
it and its shavings are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the dispute in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the shavings of a tree shaved for its own sake are permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: when a gentile shaves the idol for its sake, the idol is forbidden but its shavings are permitted.

steps.title: רב and שמואל on an idol that broke
steps.stepSummary: רב says each broken piece of an idol needs its own nullification. שמואל ties the idol's nullification to its natural form.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about an idol that broke, רב says each and every sliver must be nullified. שמואל says an idol is nullified only in the way it naturally grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a new argument: what happens when an idol breaks into pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that every broken piece keeps the idol status, so each piece needs its own nullification. שמואל disagrees and ties nullification to דרך גדילתה, the way the idol naturally grows. The גמרא explains his view in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliver or chip of wood
The way it naturally grows, its natural form

phrases.english: It was stated: an idol that broke,
Rav says: one must nullify
each and every sliver,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵינָהּ בְּטֵלָה
phrases.english: and Shmuel says: an idol is not nullified
except in the manner of its growth.
phrases.notes: A hard phrase. It links the idol's status to its natural, whole form, and the גמרא explains it next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic: idols that broke, instead of idols that were shaved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: each broken sliver needs nullification. שמואל: an idol's nullification depends on its natural form.

steps.title: Does natural growth really nullify an idol?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's wording. Something that comes off in the natural way of growing is exactly the case where the idol is NOT nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Does an idol become nullified through its natural way of growing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way שמואל's statement was worded. It sounds backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל seemed to say that an idol is nullified when it breaks in the course of its natural growth. But when leaves fall off a worshipped tree, nobody thinks the tree lost its power, so that is exactly when the idol should stay forbidden. The plain wording cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite makes more sense
Its natural way of growing (like leaves falling off a tree)
Becomes nullified, loses its idol status

phrases.english: On the contrary,
does it become nullified through its natural manner of growth?
phrases.notes: This is aimed at the wording of שמואל's statement from the end of the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of שמואל's statement in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement linking nullification to דרך גדילתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something lost through natural growth does not make the idol look powerless, so it should not nullify the idol. The wording seems reversed.

steps.title: Rereading שמואל: only natural growth needs nullification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads שמואל. A broken idol is nullified automatically. Only a piece that comes off through natural growth still needs an active nullification.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what שמואל means: an idol does not need to be actively nullified, except when a piece came off in its natural way of growing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by explaining what שמואל really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an idol truly breaks, its worshipper sees that it is powerless, so it is nullified by itself. When something falls off naturally, like leaves, the worshipper does not think less of it, so it still needs a real act of nullification. This flips the rule into the logical direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he means (a rereading of a statement)
To nullify, to cancel an idol's status by an act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'natural growth nullifies the idol.' It means the opposite: only in the natural-growth case is an active nullification still needed.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
An idol does not need to be nullified
except when it comes apart in its natural manner of growth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by rereading שמואל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל said natural growth nullifies the idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: A broken idol is nullified automatically. Only pieces that come off through natural growth still need active nullification.

steps.title: Suggestion: do they argue about worshipping fragments?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל argue about whether people worship broken fragments of idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is their argument? רב holds that people worship fragments, and שמואל holds that people do not worship fragments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind the argument between רב and שמואל. This sets up the next move, where the proposal will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people worship fragments, a broken idol is still worshipped, so each piece needs its own nullification, as רב says. If people do not worship fragments, breaking ends the idol's status, as שמואל says.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is what they argue about?

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds: people worship fragments,
phrases.notes: This first 'Sage' is רב, and the second one is שמואל.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds: people do not worship fragments?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that שמואל's view is clear, the גמרא looks for the root of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying principle divides רב and שמואל?

steps.title: No: everyone agrees fragments are worshipped; the argument is about pieces of pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both agree people worship fragments. They argue only about fragments of fragments.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that people worship fragments. Here they argue about fragments of fragments. רב holds they are forbidden, and שמואל holds they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion and moves the argument to a smaller case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both Sages agree that a broken idol's pieces can still be worshipped. The question is what happens when those pieces break again into smaller bits. רב keeps even those forbidden, while שמואל says that people do not worship such tiny bits.

keyTerms.meaning: Fragments of fragments, pieces broken off pieces

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that people worship fragments,
and here they disagree about fragments of fragments,
one Sage holds: fragments of fragments are forbidden,
and one Sage holds: fragments of fragments are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 20 and redefines the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that they argue about whether fragments are worshipped at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both Sages agree fragments are worshipped. The real argument is about smaller pieces broken from those fragments.

steps.title: Another option: an idol made of parts that anyone can reassemble
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both agree fragments of fragments are permitted. They argue about an idol built of sections that an ordinary person can put back together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: everyone agrees that fragments of fragments are permitted. They argue about an idol made of sections that an ordinary person can reassemble. רב holds that since a layman can put it back, it is not nullified. שמואל holds that an idol only needs nullification when something comes off in its natural growth, which is its normal way. Taking it apart is not natural growth, so no nullification is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the case is an idol that comes apart into sections and can easily be reassembled. רב says that because it can so easily be whole again, it keeps its idol status. שמואל applies his rule: only natural-growth separation needs active nullification, and coming apart is not natural growth, so it is nullified on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (an alternative answer)
Sections or segments that fit together
An ordinary person, not a craftsman

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule: a broken idol is nullified by itself, unless the piece came off through natural growth. רב is stricter about pieces. The גמרא gives two ways to frame their argument: fragments of fragments, or an idol made of parts that anyone can reassemble.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone agrees that fragments of fragments are permitted,
and here it is about an idol made of sections,
which an ordinary person can reassemble, that they disagree.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּהֶדְיוֹט יָכוֹל לְהַחְזִירָהּ לָא בָּטְלָה,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: since an ordinary person can reassemble it, it is not nullified,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּטֵלָה
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: an idol does not need nullifying
phrases.notes: Read this the way step 19 explained it: active nullification is needed only in the natural-growth case.

phrases.english: except through its natural manner of growth, which is its normal way,
but this is not its natural growth,
and so it does not need to be nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שִׁבְרֵי שְׁבָרִים מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to reject step 20, as an alternative to step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Again rejects that the argument is about worshipping fragments in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument may instead be about an idol of sections that can be reassembled, and whether that counts as nullified.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter כל הצלמים
steps.stepSummary: The third פרק of מסכת עבודה זרה, called כל הצלמים, comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'כל הצלמים'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the third פרק with the traditional closing line. The discussion of broken idols from the previous steps is now finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פרק is named after its opening words. The הדרן is a closing formula and does not add any new הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a פרק
'All the images': the name of the third פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All the images.'
phrases.notes: 'כל הצלמים' is the name of the פרק we just finished, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק, including the רב/שמואל discussion in steps 17–22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third פרק of עבודה זרה is complete.

steps.title: Stones lying next to the idol Mercury
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה gives two opinions about stones found next to מרקוליס. רבי ישמעאל says three stones are forbidden and two are allowed. חכמים say stones that look like part of the idol are forbidden and others are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: three stones next to each other, beside מרקוליס, are forbidden, but two are allowed. חכמים say: stones that look like they belong with it are forbidden, and stones that don't look like they belong with it are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth פרק opens with a new משנה. It presents an argument about when loose stones near the idol מרקוליס become forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל uses a number test: three stones together are forbidden, two are not. חכמים use a looks test: what counts is whether the stones appear to be part of the idol's pile. The גמרא will next try to find the reasoning behind each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here, the opening משנה of the new פרק)
Mercury, an idol worshipped by throwing stones at it
They look like they belong with it (the idol)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Three stones, one next to the other,
beside Mercury, are forbidden,
but two are allowed.
And the Rabbis say:
those that look like they belong with it are forbidden,
and those that do not look like they belong with it are allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: שָׁלֹשׁ אֲבָנִים זוֹ בְּצַד זוֹ בְּצַד מַרְקוּלִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: three adjacent stones beside מרקוליס are forbidden and two are allowed. חכמים: stones that look connected to the idol are forbidden, and others are allowed.

steps.title: The Rabbis' view makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that חכמים hold people worship broken pieces of idols. So stones that may have fallen off the idol's pile are forbidden, and stones that clearly did not are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable according to רבנן: they hold that people worship broken pieces. So stones that look like they belong with the idol, where we can say they fell off it, are forbidden. Stones that don't look like they belong with it are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the view of חכמים is easy to understand. This is a setup: it is preparing a challenge against רבי ישמעאל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים connect the stones to the idol through the idea of עובדין לשברים: a piece that fell off an idol is still worshipped. So the only question is whether a stone looks like it fell off. That explains their 'looks like it belongs' test.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (opens a contrast: 'this part makes sense, but...')

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at this step. A line that starts with בשלמא almost always leads into an 'אלא' challenge against the other opinion.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is understandable according to the Rabbis:
they hold that people worship broken pieces,
so those that look like they belong with it,
where one can say they fell from it, are forbidden;
those that do not look like they belong with it are allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of חכמים in the משנה, as the first half of a בשלמא challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים hold עובדין לשברים, so stones that may have fallen from the idol are forbidden.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. If people worship broken pieces, even two stones should be forbidden. If they don't, even three should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what does רבי ישמעאל hold? If people worship broken pieces, even two stones should be forbidden! If people do not worship broken pieces, even three should not be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל's rule of three stones versus two. Neither side of the 'broken pieces' question seems to explain his line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a dilemma with no way out. Once the question is about broken pieces, the number of stones should not matter. Either every fallen stone is forbidden, or none are. So drawing the line at three seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If ... if: sets up a two-sided dilemma

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yishmael, what does he hold?
If people worship broken pieces,
then even two should also be forbidden!
If people do not worship broken pieces,
then even three should also not be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא structure. Step 25 showed חכמים make sense, and now רבי ישמעאל is challenged.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's ruling in the משנה that three stones are forbidden and two are allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Under עובדין לשברים every fallen stone should be forbidden, even two. Under אין עובדין לשברים none should be, even three. A number test fits neither view.

steps.title: Stones known to have fallen from the idol are forbidden by everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if we know the stones fell off the מרקוליס, all opinions agree they are forbidden. Even the view that people do not worship broken pieces agrees, because loose stones are the normal way this idol exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If we know the stones fell off the מרקוליס, everyone agrees they are forbidden. Even the one who says people do not worship broken pieces only means a normal idol, where being broken is not its usual form. But here, the idol was made of separate stones from the very beginning, so loose stones are its usual form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to the question on רבי ישמעאל. First it sets aside one case where there is no argument at all: stones that we know fell off the idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 26 depended on the rule about broken pieces of idols. רבי יוחנן says that rule does not matter for stones we know came from a מרקוליס. A normal idol that breaks is no longer in its usual form, but a מרקוליס is a heap of separate stones to begin with. So a stone that fell from it is still part of the idol, and it is forbidden according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this case shows that people worship broken pieces in general. The point is that a מרקוליס is special, because its stones were separate from the start.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Where it is known that they fell from it,
everyone agrees they are forbidden.
And even according to the one who says:
People do not worship broken pieces,
that applies only to an idol
where being broken is not its normal form.
But here, where from the very beginning
they are broken pieces, that is its normal form.
phrases.notes: Literally "they are broken, broken." A מרקוליס is a heap of separate stones, so being in pieces is simply how it looks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the challenge from step 26 by removing the known-fallen case from the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stones known to have fallen from a מרקוליס are forbidden according to all opinions, since loose stones are the normal form of this idol.

steps.title: The argument is only about stones of unknown origin
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל and חכמים argue only when we do not know whether the stones came from the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is in an unknown case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The argument in the משנה is only about stones when we do not know where they came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 26 assumed the dispute was about the rule of broken pieces. Now the dispute is moved to a question of doubt: did these stones come from the idol or not? So רבי ישמעאל's numbers, three forbidden and two allowed, are about judging that doubt, not about whether broken pieces are worshipped.

keyTerms.meaning: an unknown case, where we do not know the facts

steps.whatToRemember: Stones known to have fallen from a מרקוליס are forbidden by everyone. רבי ישמעאל and חכמים argue only about stones of unknown origin.

phrases.english: Where they argue is in an unknown case.
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי ישמעאל and חכמים from the משנה, arguing about stones when nobody knows if they fell from the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 27 by saying exactly which case the dispute is about.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's split between two stones and three stones (step 26)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the dispute is only about stones whose origin is unknown
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute between רבי ישמעאל and חכמים was about whether people worship broken pieces, so his number split made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Stones known to have fallen are forbidden by everyone. The dispute is only about doubtful stones, so the number split is about judging whether they came from the idol.
